title: Rochester Man Pleads Guilty in Multiple Officer Assaults - KROC-AM
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - A Rochester man with a long history of alleged attacks on law enforcement officers has entered guilty pleas to charges in five of the cases against him. Under the terms of a plea agreement filed in Olmsted County Court, 33-year-old Mahamed Adan Abikar has admitted to four counts of felony fourth-degree assault involving law enforcement and one count of fifth-degree assault. He is scheduled to be sentenced in November. The guilty pleas stem from incidents dating back to 2022, when he was accused of kicking a Rochester police officer in the abdomen during a response to a report of a disorderly man. The following year, Abikar was charged with kicking another officer in the groin while he was allegedly resisting arrest. Abikar's cases also cover an alleged attack on a detention deputy in the Olmsted County jail in 2023 and another incident in the jail in 2024 when he was accused of spitting into the mouth of a detention deputy. His other guilty plea stems from an assault on a Rochester police officer in the downtown parking ramp last year, during which he allegedly struck the officer on the head with the bottom half of a broken cane and spit into the face of another officer. The plea deal indicates that felony charges stemming from three other incidents will be dismissed.

title: Duluth To Host 2027 IIHF U-18 World Hockey Championship - Duluth Country Radio
content: It was announced today that Duluth will be the host city for an international sporting event next year. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF), in conjunction with several local and regional representatives, announced Thursday morning at AMSOIL Arena that the 2027 IIHF Under-18 Championship tournament will be coming to the Northland next spring. The IIHF hosted its World Juniors event in Minnesota at the beginning of 2026, with Duluth being one of the cities that hosted exhibition games before the tournament in the Twin Cities. During the announcement event on Thursday morning, Minnesota Sports and Entertainment President and CEO Wendy Blackshaw commented that she and her organization were "blown away" by Duluth's participation and welcoming spirit for the exhibition games. She went on to express the hope that continues with the upcoming Under-18 tournament, saying, "Let's remind the world why we are the State of Hockey", encouraging Northlanders to support the event through volunteering, attending games, and sponsorship opportunities. Duluth Mayor Roger Reinert shared remarks during the event about how Duluth has a history of hosting world-class events, pointing to Grandma's Marathon as a prime example. He says hosting the IIHF U-18 event in the Spring of 2027 will give Duluth another way to showcase the area and welcome others from around the world. Just like with Grandma's Marathon, he is inviting community members to be part of volunteer opportunities around this event and be good ambassadors for the area as visitors arrive. USA Hockey executive director Pat Kelleher commented via a written release, saying, “Duluth is one of America’s great hockey communities and an ideal setting for this tournament. Fans will have the chance to experience elite international competition and see many of the future stars of the NHL competing on a world stage for the first time.” As highlighted by USA Hockey Assistant Executive Director Tony Driscoll, NHL talent like Quinn Hughes and Matt Boldy, along with local names like Max & Victor Plante have all played in U-18 tournaments over the years. The entirety of the 2027 IIHF U-18 event will be hosted at AMSOIL Arena, with the preliminary round games getting underway on April 21. A total of 10 participating nations will be divided into two groups. Each team will play the other four teams in their group in the preliminary rounds starting April 21, with the top four teams from each group moving on to the quarterfinals on April 29, and the winners advancing to the semifinals on May 1. Group A: United States, Sweden, Latvia, Denmark, and Norway Group B: Canada, Slovakia, Finland, Belarus, and Czechia Tony Driscoll laid out the first few games for Team USA during the preliminary rounds, which include the first game on April 21 against Norway, a game against Latvia on April 23, an April 24 matchup against Sweden, and a game against Denmark on April 26. The bronze medal game and gold medal game will both be hosted on May 2, with the bronze game at AMSOIL at 1 pm, and the gold medal game at 5 pm. Single-game tickets for the preliminary rounds will go on sale to the general public on Tuesday, September 22 at 10 am, starting at $15 per ticket. In addition to single-game tickets, there will be various ticket packages, including an all-sesson package to all of the event's games, a Team USA preliminary round package for all four of the team's preliminary round games, and other packages. Tickets will be available via the IIHF website.

title: Olmsted County Declares Local Emergency After Sept. 2 Storm - 106.9 KROC
content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - The Olmsted County Board has voted to declare a state of local emergency in the aftermath of the severe storm that smashed through southeastern Minnesota on September 2. According to a news release, the declaration clears the way for local jurisdictions in Olmsted County to apply for emergency assistance from the state of Minnesota. That assistance would help defray the expenses incurred in restoring power and clearing away debris from the storm. The next step in the process will be for Olmsted County Emergency Management to request a Preliminary Damage Assessment from the Minnesota Department of Public Safety's Homeland Security and Emergency Management division. If the assessment determines the damage meets the threshold set by the state, a request for a state disaster declaration will be submitted to Gov. Tim Walz. If approved, a state disaster declaration would allow the City of Rochester and other local governments to apply for funding from the Minnesota Disaster Assistance Contingency Account, which could cover up to 75% of the cost of the emergency response. The storm system produced straight-line winds of nearly 70 mph and knocked out power to thousands of homes and businesses in the Rochester area. Rochester Public Utilities General Manager Tim McCollough now says that nearly 11,000 RPU customers experienced outages as a result of the powerful storm. The City of Rochester has reported that its personnel have responded to nearly 650 storm-related tasks, which have largely involved widespread tree and limb damage. Earlier this week, Rochester officials issued a statement indicating the cleanup process could continue for another two to three weeks.

title: Prediction: $1,000 Invested in Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC) Today Will Be Worth This Much by the End of the Decade - The Motley Fool
content: Could investors see their investment double in that time? Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM +3.00%) is one of the most important companies in the tech world, and over the past decade, its stock has been one of the best performing. It has considerably outperformed Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms over that period. That said, investing is all about the future, so what might the next few years look like for TSMC's stock? While nobody can predict for certain how a stock will perform, I wouldn't be surprised if a $1,000 investment in TSMC today was worth $1,750 to $2,000 by the end of the decade. Let's take a look at why. Almost all electronics you use daily contain semiconductor chips. While companies like Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, and others design the chips used in their products, they don't manufacture them in-house. They outsource that to foundries, and TSMC is the No. 1 company bringing those designs to life. Manufacturing high-end processing chips requires huge investments into specialized factories and equipment, as well as a degree of expertise that comes only with time, so it's much easier for tech companies to pay TSMC for its capabilities than to try to build their own foundries. TSMC has a market share of around 73% in the global third-party foundry market (up from 68% at the start of 2025), but for advanced chips, its market share is well into the upper-90% range. That isn't by chance. TSMC is regarded as the gold standard in chip manufacturing, which is why it's the go-to partner for virtually all major tech companies. TSMC already boasts a market cap of over $2.1 trillion, and for a company of that size, doubling in value in roughly three years and three months would be unusually tough, but in this case, the premise is definitely not far-fetched. For illustration's sake, if we assume it finishes the year where it is now, it would need to average an annualized growth rate of around 26% for the next three years to double. For the more modest 75% growth that it would take to turn $1,000 into $1,750, it would need to average an annualized growth rate of around 20.5%. For perspective, TSMC's stock is up 368% over the past three years and 255% over the past five years. And while past performance doesn't guarantee future results, TSMC's business is in a great spot. First, it directly benefits from the hundreds of billions of dollars that hyperscalers Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta are spending every year to build data centers and other AI infrastructure. Most of the advanced processors at the heart of those data centers are made by TSMC. With TSMC sitting at the foundation of the broader AI boom, I can see it carrying its recent momentum over the next three years. Only time will tell how much a $1,000 investment will be worth at the end of this decade, but I can almost guarantee you won't regret making it. title: Scandia Marks 51 Years Of Taco Daze, The Labor Day Weekend Tradition Born From A 1975 Boy Scout Taco Sale - minnesotasnewcountry.com
content: As we get ready to embrace fall officially starting next week, many town celebrations are in the books. One Minnesota city, which has a population of less than 4,000 residents, just had its yearly celebration that includes tacos and a 'running of the meatballs' which makes this 'Swedish' inspired town the place to be the weekend after Labor Day. Last Saturday, I had the chance to experience one Minnesota town festival unlike many others. The quaint city of Scandia, a few miles North of Stillwater in Washington County, hosted its 51st annual Taco Daze celebration. For a town with deep Scandinavian roots, just take a look around and note all the Dala Horse statues; the celebration seems oddly named, as you don't think about Swedish tacos. But they certainly make it work. Scandia's Taco Daze started in 1975, when the local Boy Scout troop looked for a way to fundraise and decided selling tacos was the way to do it. The whole town came together to help those kids out. Eventually, the local Lions Club took over the event, and eventually other things were added to the day, like a parade, car show, and, of course, the 'running of the meatballs'. The name of the event, the running of the meatballs, makes it sound like an actual running event, where people dress up as meatballs. However fun that sounds, that isn't what the event is. Instead, those attending the event have the opportunity to 'buy' a meatball for a chance at winning the race, and by doing so, also win some money. To me, it was similar to those rubber duck races. Sign up for the 98.1 Minnesota's New Country Newsletter Thankfully, the event doesn't use real meatballs, but they do paint golf balls brown to look like a meatball, and then send them downhill on a race course, where the winning meatball crosses the finish line at the bottom of the road. If you like to experience new things, the event is held the Saturday after Labor Day. Learn more about the event by following the celebration's social media page here.

title: Museum Closed, Cars for Sale: Here's What Happened - Amarillo Country Radio
content: One gem on Route 66 sits in a truck stop on I-40 in Glenrio, NM. It is Russell's Travel Center Museum. The museum is full of classic cars, classic motorcycles, classic gas station signs, fuel pumps, and a ton of nostalgia. Or should I say, was full of all those amazing things. Unfortunately, the museum is now closed and empty. One of the not-so-great things about social media is running across something that makes you sad during your doomscrolling. That's exactly what happened to me. I was scrolling, and I saw a car on an auction site, then another, and I realized they were cars from Russell's Travel Center Museum. Read More: Road Trip To An Amazing Car Museum on Route 66 Now the museum is closed, and the days of Russell's Travel Center are gone. According to Truckers News, TravelCenters of America (TA) purchased the truck stop at 1583 Frontage Rd 4132 in 2023. Route 66 News reported that as part of the TA sale, the Russell's Travel Center name would remain for three years. Now that the three years are up, the travel center has been officially rebranded as TA, and the contents of the free museum were removed in July 2026. Even though the museum was free, it did have a donation box. Over 15 years, $520,000 was donated to food banks in Amarillo and Tucumcari. Assiter Auctioneers is holding an online auction with 432 lots from Russell's. The auction ends on October 10, 2026. The auction preview will be Thursday, October 8, and Friday, October 9, from 9 am to 5 pm. Vehicles may be previewed at the Assiter Auction Facility at 16650 I-27 in Canyon. The other items may be previewed at the museum inside the truck stop. The museum contained many historical and collector items. There were gas station signs like Texaco and Gulf, and the classic pumps that once filled those cars. Inside, there were vintage traffic lights, street signs, movie and music memorabilia, and of course, the classic cars. The cars at the start of the auction have very low bids. However, by the time the auction closes, these beauties from yesteryear will likely go for tens of thousands of dollars. I'm sad. It was a traditional stop when my family and I traveled into New Mexico. When my husband and I first started dating, we got in the car, and I started driving. I didn't tell him where we were going; I just went west on I-40. It freaked him out a little bit, not knowing where I was taking him. I knew he liked classic cars, and it was the perfect surprise date destination. I took him to the museum, and then we had breakfast at the diner. I'm sure it was a tradition for many people. If you have the funds and the means, you can now own a piece of this museum. Read More: Glenrio, Texas; The Ghost Town That's Coming Back To Life The truck stop is still there; however, it is no longer Russell's Travel Center. It is now a TA. The museum is what made the truck stop special, and now that it's gone, it's just another stop for fuel, snacks, and a potty break.

content: Rochester, MN (KROC-AM News) - The Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce today announced the launch of a five-year economic development initiative. The news release says it will "position Rochester to compete for highly skilled workers in an increasingly competitive labor market." The campaign will promote the community's "quality of life, career opportunities, and unique strengths." The business group's statement says Momentum30 will also focus on attracting new businesses and supporting existing employers. “Momentum30 will enhance our community’s ability to attract industry and new business opportunities to the Rochester area through the addition of vital, proactive business strategies that complement the development resources and partners of our region during this exciting time of growth,” said Tom Leimer, Rochester Area Chamber of Commerce Board member, Momentum30 Advisory Committee chair, and senior vice president/general manager, Knutson Construction. The Chamber of Commerce statement also notes that it has already secured 80% of the more than $1.3 million investment needed for the Momentum30 initiative.

title: Billings Auction Features Vintage Chuck E. Cheese Arcade Games - Montana Talks
content: The late Oscar Cooke started moving a modest collection of old tractors and farm equipment to a rural property on the outskirts of Billings in 1964. Like many collectors, a few pieces here and there eventually became a lot of stuff. Soon, Cooke and his wife Marcella had assembled an authentic replica of an early Montana town. Named "Cookeville," the town at Oscar's Dreamland once had a narrow-gauge train that circled the property and an operational 1920 Ferris wheel. Oscar's Dreamland was a tourist attraction in the summer months, drawing fans with its concessions, a museum, a Model T garage, a general store, and a variety of other historic buildings and displays. Read More: Here's How You Could Win $25,000 This Fall After Oscar Cooke passed away in 1995, the IRS came calling in 1998, forcing a liquidation of much of the equipment and antiques and a name change from Oscar's Dreamland to Oscar's Park. Collectors from 44 states and 17 countries attended that auction. Today, the property retains much of the former Cookeville town, and there are still hundreds (perhaps thousands?) of pieces of history dotting the footprint. Oscar Cooke's daughter, Marcie Cooke Limpp, and her husband still own and operate Oscar's Park, which nowadays is mostly utilized as a wedding venue and for other special events. A collector in her own right, affable Marcie told me how they came to possess a collection of what appear to be early 90s Chuck E. Cheese games from the Billings location. It was a prime example of right-time, right-place. An electrician friend of Limpp's was working on the lights at Chuck E. Cheese around 15 years ago. He called her up and said, "You gotta get over here right now, and bring a truck and trailer. They're getting ready to dispose of a bunch of games." So she did. Marcie said the time has come for them to downsize a bit from their massive collection, and they'll be parting with the Chuck E. Cheese games, along with hundreds of other collectibles and antiques on October 10th. The live, in-person (and by phone) Limpp Family Auction will be hosted by Rick Young & Sons. The auction kicks off at 10 AM on October 10th at Oscar's Park, 3740 Wise Lane. While the retro Chuck E. Cheese games are what caught my eye (I mean... who wouldn't want a full-sized Skeeball machine in their basement!?), fans of antique Montana agricultural equipment and other collectibles will certainly be in attendance too.

title: Meta Looks to Slash Its AI Bill With Homegrown Silicon - TradingView
content: Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ) plans to deploy its latest in-house artificial intelligence chip in data centers during the first half of 2027. The company expects the processors to cut costs and energy use as its AI infrastructure expands, Bloomberg reported Monday. Meta is testing the third generation of its chip line, MTIA 450, code-named Arke. The company first announced its custom AI chip plans in 2023. Its next processor, MTIA 500, code-named Astrid, should complete design work in about a month. Meta expects to deploy it by the end of 2027. Meta is working with Broadcom Inc. www.benzinga.com/quote/AVGO(NASDAQ:AVGO) on chip designs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd. www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM(NYSE:TSM) on production. The effort could reduce Meta’s reliance on NVIDIA Corporation https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NVDA(NASDAQ:NVDA) processors. Yee Jiun Song, Meta’s vice president of engineering, said the custom chips aim to deliver better performance per watt and per dollar. Separately, Meta on Tuesday launched Meta One, a subscription service offering expanded AI access and premium features across Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp and Meta AI. The core experience will remain free. Meta One launches with more than 50 features and has recorded 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. Paid plans offer higher AI usage, including image and video generation, as well as tools for creators and businesses. Plans are available globally. Single-product subscriptions start at $2.99 per month, individual bundles at $7.99 and creator and business bundles at $14.99. Meta stock was little changed on Tuesday as megacap growth stocks faced a broader risk-off session. The Nasdaq fell 0.60%, while the S&P 500 lost 0.52%. The stock remains above its key long-term trend gauges. It is 11.8% above its 20-day simple moving average of $595.06 and 6.7% above its 200-day SMA of $623.64. However, momentum looks stretched. Meta’s relative strength index stands at 71.02, putting the stock in overbought territory. An RSI above 70 can signal increased pullback risk after a strong rally. The longer-term setup remains mixed. The stock still carries a death cross from December 2025, when its 50-day SMA moved below the 200-day SMA. Therefore, it could remain volatile until its longer-term averages strengthen. Key resistance sits near $673, while support is around $556.50. Meta carries a Buy consensus rating with an average price forecast of $774.58. Wedbush maintained a Neutral rating on Sept. 14 and raised its price forecast to $650. JPMorgan upgraded Meta to Overweight on Sept. 10 and raised its price forecast to $820. On Sept. 1, Wedbush maintained Neutral with a $595 price forecast. The stock trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 25.1. Meta’s Benzinga Edge scorecard shows strong Growth and Quality scores of 79.54 and 71.43, respectively. Momentum stands at 42.53, while Value is 49.76. The readings point to a growth-and-quality profile. However, moderate momentum and an overbought RSI suggest the stock could consolidate after its recent rally. The First Trust Dow Jones Internet Index Fund https://www.benzinga.com/quote/FDN(NYSE:FDN) has a 9.46% Meta weighting. The Invesco AI and Next Gen Software ETF https://www.benzinga.com/quote/IGPT(NYSE:IGPT) holds 8.91%, while the Global X Social Media ETF https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SOCL(NASDAQ:SOCL) has an 8.76% weighting. Meta’s large weight in these ETFs means fund inflows and outflows can contribute to buying or selling pressure in the stock. With that in mind, Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor, Arista Networks, Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packard Enterprise stock all sport a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). Their operating momentum makes them worth considering if the AI selloff gets overdone rather than reflects a genuine deterioration in earnings prospects. Nvidia, the AI chip leader, supplies the GPUs, networking, and software powering AI training and inference. Fiscal second-quarter data-center revenue surged 117% year over year to $89 billion, while adjusted gross margin reached 75%. Management's $108 billion Q3 revenue outlook underscores substantial demand, supporting the case for considering NVDA on a sentiment-driven pullback. Taiwan Semiconductor provides the advanced chip manufacturing essential to the AI buildout. Second-quarter revenue grew roughly 34% in U.S.-dollar terms to $40.2 billion, with gross margin reaching 67.7%. August sales subsequently increased 53% YoY, offering another encouraging demand signal as its newest manufacturing technology ramps up. Arista supplies high-speed networking that connects computing resources across AI data centers. Second-quarter revenue increased nearly 38% to $3.04 billion, while adjusted EPS climbed nearly 40%. Its 49.9% adjusted operating margin demonstrates strong profitability, and new 1.6-terabit networking platforms position Arista for increasingly demanding AI deployments. Dell supplies AI servers, storage and supporting data-center infrastructure. Fiscal second-quarter AI-server revenue doubled to $16.4 billion, while its AI-server backlog reached a record $95 billion. Management also raised its current fiscal 2027 adjusted EPS guidance to $25.50 from $17.90, providing a particularly compelling earnings-based argument for considering DELL on weakness. HPE combines AI servers, networking and hybrid-cloud infrastructure. It's fiscal third-quarter revenue most recently rose 34% to $12.2 billion, with Cloud & AI operating margin expanding to 17% from 7% a year earlier. HPE also raised its FY26 adjusted EPS guidance range to $3.75-$3.85 and free-cash-flow guidance to at least $3.75 billion, strengthening the investment case beyond AI enthusiasm. Super Micro Computer also sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) and supplies AI servers and liquid-cooled, rack-scale systems. Most recently, Super Micro's fiscal fourth-quarter sales reached $11.1 billion versus $5.8 billion a year earlier, while fiscal 2027 revenue guidance of $65-$72 billion points to substantial further expansion. For all six, the strongest buy-the-dip opportunity would pair lower share prices with resilient earnings expectations. Gradual buying is more defensible than assuming the first decline marks the bottom. title: TSMC's Strong August Revenues Signal Continued AI-Driven Chip Demand - TradingView
content: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM, or TSMC, announced its consolidated net revenues for August 2026 of approximately New Taiwan Dollar (NT$) 514.81 billion, marking a 10.1% increase from July 2026 and a 53.3% rise from August 2025. Cumulative revenues from January through August 2026 reached NT$3,386.87 billion, representing 39.3% growth compared to the same period in 2025. The latest monthly performance reflects that the company continues to benefit from strong demand for its leading-edge process technologies. High-performance computing (HPC) continues to account for the biggest share of TSMC’s business, benefiting from rising data needs and the expansion of AI applications. The platform accounted for 66% of second-quarter 2026 revenues and grew 20% sequentially. The company also saw growth across Internet of Things (IoT), Digital Consumer Electronics (“DCE”) and Automotive, with revenues increasing 4%, 5% and 15%, respectively, from the prior quarter. TSMC’s technology mix remains heavily weighted toward advanced process technologies, with 7-nanometer and below accounting for 77% of wafer revenues in the second quarter. The 2-nanometer process contributed 3%, while 3-nanometer, 5-nanometer and 7-nanometer accounted for 30%, 33% and 11%, respectively. Management continues to point to robust AI-related demand, as the AI megatrend continues to drive the need for more computing and leading-edge silicon. Strong demand signals from customers, particularly cloud service providers, continue to support TSMC’s view of a multiyear AI opportunity. The company also sees another source of silicon demand emerging from Agentic AI, which is increasing the role of CPUs in AI data centers alongside AI accelerators. TSMC is working closely with CPU customers across x86, ARM-based and RISC-V architectures to support these opportunities with advanced technologies and capacity. GlobalFoundries GFS has entered into a long-term manufacturing agreement with Monolithic Power Systems, under which MPS’ proprietary process technology will be deployed at GFS’ advanced 300mm manufacturing facility in Singapore. The collaboration is expected to help GlobalFoundries expand manufacturing capacity for critical power management solutions serving high-growth markets beginning in early 2027. The company finalized a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Research and Development Office for a $375 million R&D award to accelerate its Quantum Technology Solutions business. Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. QCOM has entered into a multi-generation collaboration with Amazon to enable customized silicon at scale for large-scale AI data centers, working together on AI inference. The companies are also developing optical connectivity solutions of up to 1.6T and future-generation solutions. Qualcomm recently expanded its Dragonwing portfolio with highly integrated platforms designed to broaden access to intelligent edge computing across consumer, commercial and industrial segments. Over the past 12 months, TSMC shares have rallied 60% compared with the industry’s 65.8% growth. TSM currently trades at a forward 12-month Price/Sales (P/S) of 10.63X compared with its historical median of 11.08X and the industry average of 11.02X. Estimates for TSMC’s earnings have seen steady upward revisions over the past three months. TSMC sports a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) at present. title: MediaTek Cranks Up Pressure on Qualcomm With Cutting-Edge Smartphone Chip - TradingView
content: Qualcomm Inc. www.benzinga.com/quote/QCOM(NASDAQ:QCOM) stock traded lower during Tuesday’s premarket session as broader risk appetite weakened. Nasdaq futures fell 0.18%, while S&P 500 futures slipped 0.23%. Qualcomm Rival MediaTek Steps Up Flagship Chip Push Qualcomm also faces fresh competitive pressure from rival MediaTek. MediaTek unveiled its Dimensity 9600 Pro on Tuesday, its first smartphone chip built using Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Ltd.’s www.benzinga.com/quote/TSM(NYSE:TSM) advanced 2-nanometer process, Reuters reported. The company also launched the Dimensity 9600M, built on a 3-nanometer process. Both target the premium smartphone market. The push directly challenges Qualcomm in high-end handsets, where premium devices and on-device AI can deliver stronger margins. MediaTek said its new 9600 Pro includes a dedicated AI processor designed to handle more complex generative AI workloads directly on smartphones. MediaTek has already gained ground. Its market value surpassed Qualcomm’s earlier this year, according to Reuters. The company now sees further room to increase its share of the flagship smartphone market as advanced hardware and AI features push device prices higher. Qualcomm traded at $179.63, well above its short-term moving averages. The stock was 6.9% above its 20-day simple moving average of $167.57 and 6.2% above its 50-day SMA of $168.68.
